clue.text: Senior nurse nursing home finds menacing

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is cradled inside the other

parts.note: in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Something about the senior nurse's choice of care home strikes someone as threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sister is a senior hospital nurse, usually in charge of a ward; the insertion lands just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something that seems threatening or suggests harm is coming.

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small or tiny
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A thin person's little girl is described as very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a weed is a feeble, scrawny person with little strength.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
racy means risque or suggestive

explanation.surface: Page one of a book seems to hint that it was copied from someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is the unauthorised copying of another's work, which is what plagiarism amounts to.

indicators.note: fed means put into the mouth, so the earlier pieces go inside the child

parts.note: a son is a male child
to ring someone is to call them on the phone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent gives a little one an onion ring to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like part of the onion ring of the surface, but it is the verb, to telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion, a kind of young onion with a small bulb.

clue.text: Hearing piece produced by organ and wind instrument

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a trumpet is a brass wind instrument

explanation.surface: A device for hearing is apparently created by combining a body part with a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is an old horn-shaped device held to the ear to aid hearing.

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name, standing for any lady

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, is imagined wearing a felt hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' points to Margaret Thatcher, but the phrase splits into a chemical symbol and a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft brimmed hat usually made of felt.

clue.text: Bank policy results in second job

parts.note: a river bank is its side
a line is a policy or official position, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A bank's rules lead to staff taking on extra work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a financial institution, but here it is the side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is an activity pursued alongside one's main occupation, a secondary job.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the blooms on display at the zoo turn out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an artificial substitute, usually inferior to the real thing.

clue.text: Irish county team's leader in Bordeaux

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The captain of an Irish county side is playing in the French city of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux' looks like the city, but it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the traditional British name for red wine from the Bordeaux region.

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A family doctor is described as helpful from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as a GP, but the words split into KIN and the first letter of 'doctor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kind is considerate and willing to help others.

clue.text: Remission of sins, a bishop's answer

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
a solution is an answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A bishop responds to a question by offering forgiveness of sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is the formal forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest.

parts.note: stock, or livestock, means farm animals such as cattle

explanation.surface: Strong, solidly built cows are being brought into the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocky means short and solidly built, broad and strong.

clue.text: Hear angry talk, then cues for actors

parts.note: to catch something said is to hear it
to have words with someone is to argue angrily

explanation.surface: Someone overhears an argument and then gets prompts for performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchwords are cue words in a script that prompt an actor's next speech.

clue.text: Hearing about contrary central point of matter in court

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hearing goes around the next piece

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court

indicators.note: contrary here means facing the other way, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: the nub of a matter is its central point

explanation.surface: A court hearing deals with the opposing side's key argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns the nub round before 'about' wraps the hearing around it. 'Hearing' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'court' and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a court or body set up to judge particular disputes.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Terriers is a nickname for soldiers of the Territorial Army, TA

explanation.surface: A dog owner is told to keep their terriers under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, whose members were nicknamed Terriers, so the word is not about dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to keep hold of it.

parts.note: taken as written
a Parisian would say un for the English a
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone is swamped while standing in a French courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' reads as a law court, but it is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood, or to swamp with more than can be handled.

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
to be up is to be in residence at university, as at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to grab a picture taken at their university.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap up something is to buy or obtain it quickly and eagerly.

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A worker at the power plant is said to keep unusual hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an irregular armed force resisting an occupier.

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: ideas can mean plans or intentions
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Proposals are drawn up to feature big fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plans' looks like the definition, but it is IDEAS; the definition is 'models'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect examples or standards, models to be copied.

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle or puzzle them
a hound is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue and his dog are puzzling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A foxhound is a breed of hound trained to hunt foxes.

clue.text: Nothing different — always moving in a single direction

parts.note: O is the zero-shaped symbol for nothing
something new is different from before
ay is an old and Scottish spelling of aye, meaning always

explanation.surface: Nothing ever changes, and it always heads the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: One-way traffic or streets allow movement in one direction only.

clue.text: In the shops, turn on the waterworks, causing a strong expression of public disapproval

definitions.text: a strong expression of public disapproval

parts.note: a new book or record is out when it is on sale
turning on the waterworks is a jokey idiom for starting to cry

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into tears while out shopping, provoking a public protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest or strong expression of anger.

clue.text: Disturbing experience in river in old Kentish town

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
Deal is a seaside town in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone has an unpleasant time by a river in a historic English town.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'in's are links; DEAL is a coastal town in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or horrible experience, especially a long one.

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a hand is a manual worker, as in a factory hand

explanation.surface: Someone is employed to help a worker on the factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like a verb, as in 'employed to', but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondhand goods have already been owned and used by someone else.

parts.note: on a golf green the pin is the flagstick

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee shot travels for a second towards the flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'Drive' look like a tee shot, but it is a spin, a short trip in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a brief pleasure trip in a car, a drive.

clue.text: Got rid of, the woman departs

parts.note: she refers to a woman
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A woman leaves, having discarded something.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off or get rid of it.

parts.note: a band is a group of people
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A gang has an Italian member.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, an outlaw.

clue.text: Astronaut's monicker is better read backwards!

indicators.note: read backwards tells us to take the pieces in reverse letter order

parts.note: a monicker is a name
to cap something is to outdo or better it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks an astronaut's nickname would be improved if spelt in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read backwards' turns NAMECAPS round as a whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceman is an informal word for an astronaut, someone who travels in space.
